title: Culture and constitutional compliance
abstract: arXiv:2608.23369v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Constitutions as the formal foundation of a country's legal and political system have important economic and political effects. Yet, we still know little about why constitutions set effective constraints on politicians in some societies, while being largely disregarded in others. Here, we ask if national culture matters for constitutional compliance. We study a cross-section of 115 countries, making use of novel indicators of constitutional compliance. We find that societies with a more individualistic population exhibit higher levels of compliance. These results are robust and extend to instrumental variables estimations. They imply a novel transmission channel from cultural traits to long-term economic development: individualistic national culture increases the credibility of constitutional self-commitments. Our analysis also supports the more general idea that the effects of formal institutions depend on the informal institutional env

translated_abstract: 摘要：宪法作为一个国家法律和政治体系的正式基础，具有重要的经济和政治影响。然而，我们仍然对为什么在某些社会中宪法能有效约束政治家，而在其他社会中却基本被忽视这一点知之甚少。在此，我们探讨国家文化是否对宪法遵守产生影响。我们利用新的宪法遵守指标，研究了115个国家的横截面数据。我们发现，人口中个人主义倾向更强的社会表现出更高的遵守水平。这些结果稳健，并扩展到工具变量估计中。它们暗示了一条从文化特征到长期经济发展的新型传导渠道：个人主义国家文化增强了宪法自我承诺的可信度。我们的分析也支持更普遍的观点，即正式制度的效果取决于非正式制度环境。
tldr: 本研究发现个人主义国家文化能显著提高宪法遵守水平，揭示了一条从文化特征到长期经济发展的新型传导渠道。
en_tdlr: This study finds that individualistic national culture significantly enhances constitutional compliance, revealing a novel transmission channel from cultural traits to long-term economic development.
